role.altitude: The chemistry lecturer keeps lecturing, demonstrating, supervising at the bench, judging reports and enforcing safety; copying safety data into risk forms, quizzing every student on safety rules by voice, checking calculations line by line and writing the same feedback again shrink.
skills_to_grow: Building structured lab report templates with checked fields
role.ambitious_version: A lecturer whose lab marking checks the arithmetic, leaving time for the chemistry.

tasks.short: Update slides and practice problems, prepare demonstrations, deliver lectures on topics such as organic chemistry, analytical chemistry and chemical separation, and answer questions.

steps.what: Lecturer updates lecture slides, structures and practice problems

loop.input: The lecture topic and the lecturer's existing problems.
loop.output: Draft practice problems with worked answers.
loop.check: The lecturer solves each problem independently and discards any whose answer differs.
loop.stop: The lecturer keeps checked problems, or writes their own when drafts fail.
loop.why_not_simpler: New problems are needed each year to avoid recycled answers.

steps.what: Lecturer delivers lectures on organic chemistry, analytical chemistry or chemical separation
Lecturer answers students' questions after the lecture

tasks.design: A drafting step proposes new practice problems with worked answers on the lecture topic, and the lecturer solves each one independently and keeps only those that check out. Demonstrations, lecturing and answering questions stay fully with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: New problems were written and solved from scratch each year.
tasks.enabler_now: Drafting of practice problems checked by the lecturer.
tasks.still_hard: Problems needing exact spectra or data.
tasks.human_edge: Showing a reaction so students remember it.

reach.learn: Whether more fresh problems help learning.

evidence.claim: Drafting course materials is not a high-risk use; grading and proctoring are.

assumptions: Boundary: preparing and delivering lectures; course materials such as syllabi and handouts (task 5873) are a sibling task.
Demonstrations, lecturing and answering keep their full time.
unknowns: How often problem sets are renewed.
research_questions: Does preparation time fall without errors in problems?

already_counted.description: Lecturer solves drafted problems to check them.

incremental.description: Lecturer files checked problems in the course library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few drafted problems survive the lecturer's own solving, so s1 keeps 90 (2.3); high: drafts usable as assumed (6.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Establish safety rules and risk forms for experiments, teach the rules, check students' knowledge with a pre-lab quiz, and monitor students' compliance with safety rules for handling chemicals and equipment.

steps.what: Student completes the pre-lab safety quiz in the learning platform
Lecturer establishes safety rules and the risk form for each experiment
Lecturer teaches the safety rules for handling chemicals, equipment and hazardous materials
Lecturer checks that each student knows the rules before entering the lab
Lecturer monitors students' compliance with safety rules in the lab

tasks.design: The risk form for each experiment pulls hazard statements and protective measures from the safety data sheets in the chemical inventory, and the lecturer adds the experiment-specific rules, instead of copying them by hand. Students take an auto-marked pre-lab quiz on closed questions in the learning platform; the lecturer sees who passed instead of quizzing each student at the door. Teaching the rules and watching the lab stay fully with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Safety data were copied by hand and knowledge checked orally.
tasks.enabler_now: Chemical inventories with safety data and auto-marked closed-question quizzes.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a student about to pipette by mouth.
tasks.altitude: Less copying and quizzing; supervision stays.

reach.learn: Whether risk forms are complete before each practical.

evidence.claim: An assessment platform auto-marks closed questions without AI.

assumptions: Boundary: safety rules; selecting and maintaining chemicals and supplies (task 20072) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s2: safety data sheets kept in the chemical inventory by the lab technicians.
Students' quiz time is shown in s1 and is about what the oral check took them.
Teaching and monitoring keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of different experiments per year.
research_questions: Do safety incidents in student labs fall?

incremental.description: Lecturer keeps quiz questions in line with current rules.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: safety data sheets are missing from the inventory for many chemicals, so s2 keeps 85 (13.7); high: sheets in the inventory as assumed (18.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check lab report calculations and format, assess laboratory performance, evaluate and grade class work, assignments and papers against the rubric, and write feedback.

steps.what: Students enter yields, concentrations and other numeric results in the report template's fields
Lecturer checks lab report calculations, units and format: every report by hand today, only results flagged by the range check after the change
Lecturer evaluates and grades class work, assignments and papers against the rubric

loop.input: The lecturer's short notes and rubric scores per student.
loop.output: Draft feedback text per rubric item.
loop.check: Each comment must reflect the lecturer's note and score; the lecturer checks that each comment says what the note says about this student's work and edits it; unclear comments are written by hand.
loop.stop: The lecturer writes the feedback by hand when the draft misses the point.
loop.why_not_simpler: Feedback must speak to each student's own mistakes.

steps.what: Lecturer checks the final feedback per student: each comment fits that student's report and grade
Lecturer releases the checked feedback to the students in the learning platform

tasks.design: Lab reports use a structured template in the learning platform where yields, concentrations and other numeric results are entered in fields; code checks them against the expected value range and units and checks citation format, so the lecturer looks only at flagged results. Assessing lab performance and grading stay with the lecturer; no software sets a grade. Feedback is drafted from the lecturer's own notes and rubric scores, edited, checked per student and released once.

approvals.approved_version: The feedback per student exactly as checked by the lecturer in s4b, released once to each student in the learning platform; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Every calculation was checked by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured report templates with code checks and feedback drafted from instructor notes.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing why a student's yield is low from the procedure they describe.

evidence.claim: A learning platform drafts text and rubric feedback from instructor notes.
In a randomised trial assistants agreed with 88% of AI feedback judgments and revisions improved; no time data.
Examiners appointed by the examination board set results, so no software sets a grade.

assumptions: Boundary: grading class work and reports; examinations (task 5871) and grade records (task 5872) are sibling tasks.

Assessing and grading keep their full time. Students' entry of results in fields (s0) replaces writing them in free text. s1 keeps 50 for flagged results and format; s4 keeps 70 because the lecturer edits every comment; checking and releasing feedback keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of reports with structured numeric results.
research_questions: Is feedback returned sooner without lower quality?

incremental.description: Lecturer sets expected value ranges per experiment.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: students fill the fields inconsistently, so most reports are still checked by hand and s1 keeps 80 (9.8); high: range checks flag only a few results as assumed (17.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check the lab is ready, supervise students' laboratory work at the bench, and sign off their results.

steps.what: Lecturer checks that equipment and chemicals are ready for the session
Lecturer supervises students' laboratory work at the bench
Lecturer signs off students' results in their lab notebooks

tasks.design: Nothing changes in this task. Checking the lab, supervising at the bench and signing off results stay with the lecturer; signing in an electronic notebook takes about as long as initialling a paper one, so no saving is claimed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results were signed in paper notebooks.
tasks.still_hard: Wet or contaminated benches where tablets are unsuitable.
tasks.human_edge: Stepping in before a student heats a closed system.

reach.learn: Whether notebooks are complete when reports are due.

evidence.claim: Electronic lab notebooks let supervisors sign off entries.

assumptions: Boundary: supervising lab work; maintaining chemicals and supplies (task 20072) is a sibling task.
s1 is a hands-on check that equipment and chemicals are ready and keeps its full time.
unknowns: Whether the teaching lab has bench tablets.
research_questions: Are sign-offs faster at the end of a session?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Nothing changes: checking the lab, supervising at the bench and signing results stay hands-on, so low and high are both 0.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
